max: FYI ran an offline replay against the 'last-48h-prod-trace' with the new continuous-batching heuristic tweaks we discussed (token_budget_target=256, soft queue size cap). Overall throughput looked fine but I see a clear 99.9% tail regression (~+22% latency) compared to baseline. Exported the per-model breakdown and raw traces.

replay-bot: Replay run complete: traces=48h, requests=1.2M, avg_latency=82ms, p95=140ms, p99=410ms, p999=1280ms (baseline p999=1050ms). KV warmup hit-rate dropped from 0.74 -> 0.58 for sequences > 1024.

max: Config used (snippet):
```
batching:
  token_budget_target: 256
  max_batch_size_soft: 48
  queue_policy: age_priority_with_size_softcap
kv_cache:
  warmup_policy: lazy
  prefetch_window: 0
kernel_selector:
  prefer_int8_when_possible: true
```

tara: hmm, where is the regression concentrated? short vs long seqs? particular models?

max: Per-model quick summary:
- small-chat-v2: p999 +6%
- longgen-2b: p999 +35% (this is the big one)
- rerank-lite: no change

Breakdown by request length (tokens):
- <=256: no change
- 257-1024: small uptick
- >1024: major tail regression

chao: that smells like KV warmup interaction with the new token_budget_target. If we shorten token budget we may force more early flushes so long sequences lose prefix cache amortization.

sophia: can we verify by forcing KV prewarm for the longgen slices in replay? maybe a prewarm policy change will recover tail.

max: I ran a quick patch: set kv_cache.warmup_policy=aggressive for >1024 traces and re-ran a subset (200k requests). p999 moved from 1280ms -> 980ms for longgen-2b. So KV warmup is the dominant factor.

replay-bot: Sub-run: subset=200k, longgen-2b, old: p999=1280ms, new (aggressive warmup): p999=980ms, cost +4% tokens.

chao: tradeoff is clear: token budget tuning reduced average cost but broke amortization for very long sequences. Two levers: increase token_budget_target for requests with expected long continuation or classify by model/route. Also consider kernel switch: long sequences may benefit from alternate attention kernel (chunked attention) that has steadier per-token perf.

tara: agree. For safety I'd prefer a per-route token_budget_target override rather than global bump. We can add a rule in smart-routing/batching: if expected_length > 1024 then token_budget_target=512.

max: plan proposal: (1) run A/B using the eval harness: A=global 256 (current), B=per-route override for routes flagged as longgen (token_budget_target=512 + aggressive kv warmup). (2) include kernel selection experiment: for B, force alternate attention kernel for long sequences. (3) metric hooks: p99/p999, kv_warmup_hit_rate, token/unit cost delta. Rollout if p999 improves and cost delta < 8%.

sophia: add SLO guard to rollback if p999 regressed on other routes. Also include an ingress canary with only 2% traffic first.

chao: I can wire kernel selector flag into the replay harness to replay the same requests with both kernels for a fair compare. Need ~6h on bench cluster for 48h trace subset.

max: can someone kick off the A/B harness for a 24h subset tomorrow morning? I'll open a PR for the per-route token_budget override and add the aggressive warmup toggle.

tara: i'll run the A/B in the morning (timezone CA). will post results to this thread. quick question: do we have a deterministic map for "longgen" routes or should we infer at dispatch by first N tokens?

max: let's use dispatch heuristic for now: if prompt_len > 1024 or model in [longgen-2b, longgen-6b] tag as longgen. We'll iterate.

sophia: noted — i'll add canary alert config in the console so SRE gets paged if p999 > baseline + 15% during the experiment window.

max: thanks. volunteers for the bench run? chao offered to wire kernel tests. tara will run A/B. i'll do the PR and coordinate the canary.

tara: on it. adding a quick dashboard patch to surface kv warmup rates per-route.

max: awesome — we'll reconvene after the A/B. thanks :thumbsup:
